Because of the above stuff, I fell into a pretty bad state. I hated myself for being unable to get a job, I hated my country for making the economy so bad (this was in 2009/10/11 at the height of the recession), and I just hated the world. I felt utterly useless. Eventually I had a severe mental breakdown that almost killed my relationship with my parents permanently. I screamed for an hour and sobbed for another hour, the latter half of that wishing I could die. It was like all that work I put into education was worth nothing.

I eventually saw no other way out than to join the military. I was healthy, so they took me. I enlisted rather than tried for a commission as an officer because enlisting was easier to do. I've been in almost five years now and never looked back. It's awesome. I'm in the Air Force and not the Navy, but really, you have to pick which branch appeals most to you and the Air Force was it for me. I'm sure you'll love the Navy just as much.

So here's the big question. Should you finish your education first or do it later? I'm not gonna tell you what to do, but I will tell you the pros and cons of doing either. By finishing your education now, you'll probably promote faster and you won't have to do extra work (studying for exams, online stuff, etc.) while on the job so you're saving yourself some ass pain. At the same time, education influences your performance reports (they do in the Air Force at least) so you'll have to find other ways to better yourself so you can talk about it on paper (attending professional development courses, doing volunteer work, etc.). By dropping out now and joining up, a lot of what goes into your performance reports will be education so you'll have to do a little bit every year, and you'll have to do a lot of that stuff (writing papers, doing online discussions, etc.) not only on the job, but at home as well. The pro is that the military pays for a LOT of that stuff, so if you want to go on and do a Master's or even a Ph.D they cover a huge portion of it.

Hope that helps! And if you have any questions about military life, feel free to ask. I don't know that much about the Navy specifically, but a lot of stuff still crosses over.

Nobody can answer that question for you, because joining the military isn't for everyone just like college isn't for everyone - but you can't just leave the military if you find out it isn't the right fit. In my case, I was in pretty much the same place you are (one year of college, wasn't interested in it at all, fairly depressed), and I just left for a couple years and tried to figure out what I wanted. I did a lot of research into the branches of the military and decided that I wanted to join the Air Force, went through the process, and now I ship out in March. I'm very excited about it, and think it will be a great choice for myself and make it easier for me to get into whatever else I want to do down the line.

My suggestion would be maybe to take the ASVAB or some practice tests at military.com and see what sort of job specializations you might fit into. Look into navy.com and see what sort of jobs they offer, and see if any make you feel like they're the right thing for you. Maybe just schedule an appointment with a local recruiter and talk to them about your options - they don't make you sign up for the military just to answer a few questions (but beware, it is their job to tell you what they can to get you to sign up and they will obviously put that first). I found my trip to the recruiter to be enlightening and being able to look through the jobs and find what I wanted was great. Another thing to keep in mind, though, is that you will not ever be promised a job until you sign the contract for that job (unless you join the Army, or so I heard at MEPS).

If you go through it all and decide to enlist, then awesome, but make sure that before you take your ASVAB, you do the study tests at military.com. I did those after getting a 78 AFQT on the practice test at the recruiter's office, and when I went in for the actual test I scored a 94 AFQT. The practice tests are really long and incredibly helpful.

I'm not sure if any of this has been helpful at all, but it's critical that you not let anyone make this big of a decision for you. The only thing I recommend for sure is that you take some time to think about all your options before jumping into any of them - spending aimless time in college will get you into debt, and joining the military can land you with eight years of regret if it isn't right for you. Oh, and also another thing - I have found that getting a workout routine and getting into shape is one of the greatest feelings in the world. Regardless of what decision you make, make the decision to get into shape and do it. You will be better off for it no matter where you go in life.

I have to say, I never worked out a day, or did any really helpful extra-curricular activities (Latin Club and theater in HS, pretty self-serving), but now that I've been working out, and actually getting out in the world, It feels really good. You have been a help, thanks.
